knowledge_base.title: When to use interproximal reduction
knowledge_base.body: Interproximal reduction (IPR) creates space by removing a small amount of enamel between adjacent teeth, typically 0.2-0.5mm per contact. Use it for mild to moderate crowding where arch expansion alone will not resolve the discrepancy, and for correcting Bolton discrepancies in tooth-size ratio. Stage IPR according to the treatment plan rather than performing it all up front, and never exceed the total enamel reduction specified in the plan.

knowledge_base.title: Attachment placement basics
knowledge_base.body: Attachments are small composite shapes bonded to the tooth surface to give aligners a grip point for movements the aligner cannot otherwise produce, such as extrusion and rotation. Isolate and etch the tooth thoroughly before bonding; contamination is the most common cause of attachments failing in the first week. If an attachment debonds mid-treatment, rebond it using the original template before the patient advances to the next aligner.

knowledge_base.title: Handling refinement requests
knowledge_base.body: A refinement is a new set of aligners produced after the initial series, used when the achieved tooth positions differ from the planned positions. Take fresh scans only once the patient has worn the final aligner for at least two weeks so the teeth have settled. Submit refinement scans with a note describing which movements did not track, since that materially changes how the new series is planned.

knowledge_base.title: Cleaning and daily care of aligners
knowledge_base.body: Rinse aligners in lukewarm water each time they are removed and brush them gently with a soft brush and clear unscented soap. Hot water distorts the thermoplastic and will ruin the fit permanently, so never use boiling water or a dishwasher. Patients should wear aligners 20-22 hours a day and store them in the case rather than in a napkin.
